fullTextEN: Hi, everyone!
I am Nika.
I come from China.
I live in Hefei, Anhui Province.

fullTextZH: 今天我们聊两个快餐店品牌。
fullTextEN: Today we talk about two fast food brands.
KFC and McDonald's.

fullTextZH: 这两家店在很多国家都有。
fullTextEN: These two stores are in many countries.
So in China,

fullTextZH: 肯德基和麦当劳谁更受欢迎？
fullTextEN: Which is more popular, KFC or McDonald's?
Some friends might think,
McDonald's is very famous worldwide,

fullTextZH: 肯定是麦当劳更受欢迎吧？
fullTextEN: Surely McDonald's is more popular?
But what is the answer?
Let's find out together.
Globally speaking,
McDonald's is indeed number one.

fullTextZH: 麦当劳在全世界120多个国家和地区，
fullTextEN: McDonald's is in over 120 countries and regions worldwide,

fullTextZH: 一共有超过4万家的门店。
fullTextEN: with more than 40,000 stores in total.

fullTextZH: 而肯德基大概是2万多家，
fullTextEN: While KFC has about over 20,000 stores,

fullTextZH: 比麦当劳少了差不多一半。
fullTextEN: That's about half as much as McDonald's.
So, in comparison worldwide,
McDonald's has more stores,
and is more popular.

fullTextZH: 但是，中国是一个很特别的地方，
fullTextEN: However, China is a very special place,
It has its own rules.
"First come, first served" is very important here.

fullTextZH: 肯德基比麦当劳早三年进入中国。
fullTextEN: KFC entered China three years before McDonald's.
Hmm, it's these three years,

fullTextZH: 让肯德基在中国发展得很快。
fullTextEN: that allowed KFC to develop quickly in China.

fullTextZH: 为什么这三年这么重要？
fullTextEN: Why are these three years so important?
Because over 30 years ago in China,

fullTextZH: 中国人对外国食物还很陌生，
fullTextEN: Chinese people were still unfamiliar with foreign food,

fullTextZH: 不太知道外国食物是什么。
fullTextEN: and didn't really know what foreign food was.
So, whoever appeared first,
we would remember them first.

fullTextZH: 这就像我们认识新朋友，
fullTextEN: It's like when we meet new friends,

fullTextZH: 第一个和你打招呼、和你聊天的人，
fullTextEN: the first person to greet and chat with you,
you will definitely remember them clearly,
right?

fullTextZH: 现在，我们把时间倒回1987年。
fullTextEN: Now, let's turn back time to 1987.
For many Chinese people,
this year was an ordinary year.
But for Chinese dining,
it was a special year.
Because in this year,

fullTextZH: 中国第一家肯德基开业了，
fullTextEN: China's first KFC opened,
right in the center of Beijing,

fullTextZH: 最繁华的王府井大街上，
fullTextEN: on the bustling Wangfujing Street,
very close to Tiananmen Square.

fullTextZH: 王府井大街是北京最重要、
fullTextEN: Wangfujing Street is Beijing's most important,

fullTextZH: 历史最久的商业街之一，
fullTextEN: and one of the oldest commercial streets,

fullTextZH: 已经有几百年的历史了。
fullTextEN: with a history of several hundred years.
Every day,

fullTextZH: 都会有全国各地的人到那去逛街、购物。
fullTextEN: people from all over the country would go there to stroll and shop.

fullTextZH: 而且，那时候的王府井大街，
fullTextEN: Moreover, at that time, Wangfujing Street,

fullTextZH: 嗯，主要呢是卖传统的东西，
fullTextEN: um, mainly sold traditional things,
such as silk, tea, and so on.

fullTextZH: 突然有一家卖炸鸡、汉堡的外国餐厅，
fullTextEN: Suddenly, a foreign restaurant selling fried chicken and burgers,

fullTextZH: 一下子就得到了大家的注意。
fullTextEN: immediately caught everyone's attention.

fullTextZH: 这家肯德基开业那天，9点才开门，
fullTextEN: On the day this KFC opened, it didn't open until 9 o'clock,
but around 6 in the morning,

fullTextZH: 就有人在餐厅门口排队了。
fullTextEN: there were already people lining up at the restaurant entrance.
By the time it opened,

fullTextZH: 排的队伍已经绕了餐厅两圈，
fullTextEN: the line had already wrapped around the restaurant twice,
stretching several hundred meters long.
Many people were from out of town,

fullTextZH: 就为了尝一尝外国餐厅是什么味道。
fullTextEN: just to taste what a foreign restaurant was like.

fullTextZH: 那时候，对于大多数中国人来说，
fullTextEN: At that time, for most Chinese people,
KFC was definitely not fast food,
but a high-end restaurant,
which means a very expensive restaurant.
Why do we say this?
Because at that time,
Chinese people's income was not high,

fullTextZH: 平时吃饭都是在家里做，
fullTextEN: and usually meals were cooked at home,
or at small restaurants.

fullTextZH: 这在当时对于中国人来说是很少见的、
fullTextEN: This was very rare and new for Chinese people at that time,
a very new thing.

fullTextZH: 所以，年轻人会把这里当成约会的地方。
fullTextEN: So, young people would treat it as a dating place.
Yes, they went to KFC for a date.

fullTextZH: 男生带女生去肯德基吃一顿，
fullTextEN: The boy takes the girl to KFC for a meal,
It's definitely very prestigious,
a very romantic thing.

fullTextZH: 比较有钱的爸爸妈妈如果高兴，
fullTextEN: If wealthier parents are happy,

fullTextZH: 也会把孩子带去肯德基过生日。
fullTextEN: they will also take their kids to KFC for birthdays.

fullTextZH: 很多小朋友的愿望就是去过生日、
fullTextEN: Many children's wish is to have a birthday,
and eat KFC.

fullTextZH: 那个时候的肯德基里有很多拍照的人，
fullTextEN: At that time, there were many people taking photos in KFC,
like a famous tourist spot.
So, why was KFC considered a high-end restaurant by Chinese people at that time?

fullTextZH: 肯德基对中国人来说是高级餐厅呢？
fullTextEN: KFC was considered a high-end restaurant by Chinese people?

fullTextZH: 那时候，城市里的中国人
fullTextEN: At that time, the average monthly salary of urban Chinese people

fullTextZH: 平均月薪大约是70元人民币。
fullTextEN: was about 70 yuan.

fullTextZH: 而当时吃一顿肯德基要多少钱呢？
fullTextEN: And how much did a meal at KFC cost back then?
A hamburger was 9 yuan;
a portion of chicken nuggets was 6 yuan;
a cup of cola was 3 yuan.
If two people went for a meal,
ordering two hamburgers,
One order of chicken nuggets,
Two cups of cola,
Hmm, it costs about 30 yuan.

fullTextZH: 大约等于一个中国人半个月的工资。
fullTextEN: Approximately equal to half a month's salary for a Chinese person.

fullTextZH: 所以，在当时，很多家庭都是存了很久
fullTextEN: So, at that time, many families saved for a long time

fullTextZH: 的钱，才敢带孩子去一次。
fullTextEN: before daring to take their children once.

fullTextZH: 肯德基在中国开了三年之后，
fullTextEN: Three years after KFC opened in China,
McDonald's came to China.

fullTextZH: 中国第一家麦当劳餐厅在深圳开业。
fullTextEN: the first McDonald's restaurant in China opened in Shenzhen.
At that time, Shenzhen

fullTextZH: 有很多外国人和做生意的人，
fullTextEN: had many foreigners and business people,
Hmm, so,
McDonald's chose to open here
its first store in China.

fullTextZH: 当中国的第一家麦当劳开业的时候，
fullTextEN: When the first McDonald's in China opened,

fullTextZH: 中国人已经通过肯德基知道了汉堡、
fullTextEN: Chinese people already knew about hamburgers
and the taste of fried chicken and cola.

fullTextZH: 所以，麦当劳并没有像肯德基那样
fullTextEN: So, McDonald's did not bring the first surprise
like KFC did.

fullTextZH: 而且，当时肯德基已经在全中国开分店，
fullTextEN: Moreover, at that time, KFC had already opened branches all over China,
except for Beijing,
Shanghai,

fullTextZH: 广州等大城市也慢慢开了肯德基餐厅。
fullTextEN: and other big cities like Guangzhou also gradually opened KFC restaurants.
As for McDonald's, until 1992,

fullTextZH: 才在北京开了中国的第二家店，
fullTextEN: it only opened its second store in China in Beijing,

fullTextZH: 开店速度比肯德基慢了很多。
fullTextEN: opening stores much slower than KFC.

fullTextZH: 麦当劳更强调自己的美国文化，
fullTextEN: McDonald's emphasized its American culture more,

fullTextZH: 菜单上的食物和美国的差不多。
fullTextEN: and the food on the menu was similar to that in America.
As for KFC,

fullTextZH: 已经开始尝试为中国人做一些改变。
fullTextEN: it had already started trying to make some changes for Chinese people.

fullTextZH: 比如，肯德基的菜单里有蔬菜，
fullTextEN: For example, KFC's menu included vegetables,

fullTextZH: 因为中国人爱吃蔬菜的习惯。
fullTextEN: because of the Chinese habit of loving to eat vegetables.

fullTextZH: 这也让肯德基在当时啊，
fullTextEN: This also made KFC more popular among Chinese people at that time,
um, more welcomed by Chinese people.

fullTextZH: 中国人觉得早餐很重要，
fullTextEN: Chinese people think breakfast is very important,
and they like to eat hot food,

fullTextZH: 比如粥、豆浆、油条、包子等等。
fullTextEN: such as porridge, soy milk, fried dough sticks, buns, etc.

fullTextZH: 肯德基和麦当劳一开始呢，
fullTextEN: KFC and McDonald's at first,

fullTextZH: 在中国卖的早餐和在国外一样，
fullTextEN: sold breakfasts in China that were the same as abroad,
For example, bread, hamburgers, coffee.
But they didn't sell well.
Later,

fullTextZH: 他们发现中国人早上不喜欢吃这些，
fullTextEN: They found that Chinese people don't like to eat these in the morning,

fullTextZH: 于是就开始试着卖中国的早餐。
fullTextEN: So they started trying to sell Chinese breakfast.

fullTextZH: 肯德基是最早这么做的。
fullTextEN: KFC was the first to do this.

fullTextZH: 2002年，肯德基推出了自己的中式早餐，
fullTextEN: In 2002, KFC launched its own Chinese-style breakfast,

fullTextZH: 第一个产品就是粥和豆浆。
fullTextEN: The first products were porridge and soy milk.
As soon as these two products were launched,
many people liked them.
Many working people,

fullTextZH: 早上没有时间在家里做早餐，
fullTextEN: don't have time to make breakfast at home in the morning,

fullTextZH: 就会去肯德基买一碗粥和一杯豆浆，
fullTextEN: so they go to KFC to buy a bowl of porridge and a cup of soy milk,

fullTextZH: 既方便，又符合自己的口味。
fullTextEN: which is both convenient and suits their taste.

fullTextZH: 看到肯德基的中式早餐卖得这么好，
fullTextEN: Seeing KFC's Chinese breakfast selling so well,

fullTextZH: 2004年，麦当劳推出了自己的中式早餐，
fullTextEN: In 2004, McDonald's launched its own Chinese-style breakfast,

fullTextZH: 嗯，比如菜肉粥、豆浆等等，
fullTextEN: Hmm, like vegetable meat porridge, soy milk, etc.,

fullTextZH: 但是没有肯德基卖得好。
fullTextEN: but it didn't sell as well as KFC.
KFC continuously launched

fullTextZH: 符合中国人口味的新产品。
fullTextEN: new products that suit Chinese tastes.

fullTextZH: 其中最成功、最好的一个例子，
fullTextEN: One of the most successful and best examples,

fullTextZH: 就是模仿北京烤鸭卷饼，
fullTextEN: is imitating the Beijing roast duck wrap,
and launched the 'Old Beijing Chicken Wrap'.
Wrap chicken and cucumber,

fullTextZH: 葱包在一个薄薄的面饼里面，
fullTextEN: and scallions in a thin pancake,

fullTextZH: 然后做成老北京鸡肉卷。
fullTextEN: then make it into an Old Beijing Chicken Wrap.
When you eat this,

fullTextZH: 有点像北京的烤鸭卷饼。
fullTextEN: it tastes a bit like a Beijing roast duck wrap.
As soon as this product was launched,
it immediately became popular,

fullTextZH: 直到现在还是很受欢迎。
fullTextEN: and it is still very popular now.
Many Chinese people feel that,

fullTextZH: 肯德基更懂中国人的口味，
fullTextEN: KFC understands Chinese tastes better,

fullTextZH: 也更愿意去肯德基吃饭。
fullTextEN: and are more willing to eat at KFC.
Returning to the original question,
in China, who is more popular?
From the number of stores,
KFC has more.
Moreover, when we ask Chinese people:

fullTextZH: “你吃肯德基多还是麦当劳多？”
fullTextEN: "Do you eat more KFC or McDonald's?"
Most people would say KFC.
Because KFC came early,
there are more Chinese-style foods,
and it's easier to find.

fullTextZH: 不过，麦当劳也很受欢迎，
fullTextEN: However, McDonald's is also very popular,
especially young people like it.
Many children,

fullTextZH: 还是很喜欢麦当劳的开心乐园餐，
fullTextEN: still really like McDonald's Happy Meal,
because there are toys inside.
Next time you come to China,

fullTextZH: 都可以试一试肯德基和麦当劳，
fullTextEN: you can try KFC and McDonald's,
then tell me,
which one do you like more?

fullTextEN: Alright, today's video ends here.
In your country,

fullTextZH: 麦当劳和肯德基哪个更受欢迎呢？
fullTextEN: which is more popular, McDonald's or KFC?
Why?
